children.name: Location
children.desc: These settings are independent from Obsidian's own "Default location for new attachments" under Settings → Files and links. That core setting only decides where a file lands the instant you attach it — this plugin then reorganizes it from there, right away, using the rules below.

options.label: Next to note, in folder specified below

children.desc: Folder name appended after the location above, e.g. "_sources". Only used by the "Fixed folder" and "Next to note" locations.

children.name: Attachment folder template
children.desc: Subfolder path built inside the root above. Variables: ${notepath} (note's folder + title, no extension), ${notename} (title only), ${parent} (note's parent folder name).

children.name: Attachment filename template
children.desc: New filename, without extension — the original extension is always kept as-is. Variables: ${date}, ${notename}, ${md5}, ${originalname} (the file's true original name, frozen the first time it was seen).

children.name: Date format
children.desc: Moment.js format used to render ${date} above.Example: 2026-10-22-07_41_49_SSS

children.name: Automatically rename attachment
children.desc: When you rename or move a note, move its attachments along with it and update every link that points to them, everywhere in the vault.

children.name: Clean up empty folders
children.desc: After moving an attachment out, delete its old folder if this plugin just emptied it. Never touches a folder that still holds a note or other files.

children.name: Scan frontmatter properties for attachment links
children.desc: Also treat file links written as [[wikilink]] inside frontmatter properties as attachments belonging to the note (not just links in the note body). A plain-string path property (without [[double brackets]]) still can't be detected either way.

children.name: Disable notifications
children.desc: Hide the small popup shown after attachments are organized (e.g. "Organized 3 attachments"). Errors are still printed to the developer console either way.

children.name: Debug logging
children.desc: Print detailed step-by-step logs to the developer console, prefixed [attachment-steward]. Open the console with Cmd+Option+I (Mac) or Ctrl+Shift+I (Windows/Linux). Leave off for everyday use - it's noisy.

children.name: Extension overrides
children.desc: Use a different folder/filename template for specific file extensions - e.g. keep PDFs in their own folder, separate from images. The extension field is a regular expression (case-insensitive), so e.g. "jpe?g|png|gif|webp" matches several extensions in one row.

children.name: Managed attachments
children.desc: 0 tracked

children.name: Reapply rules to all managed attachments
children.desc: Recomputes the destination of every attachment already tracked by this plugin, from its frozen original name. Doesn't discover new attachments or assign owners - use Adopt below for that.

children.name: Reapply rules to active note's attachments
children.desc: Same as above, limited to attachments already owned by the currently open note.

children.name: Adopt unmanaged attachments in active note
children.desc: Scans links and embeds in the active note (plus frontmatter [[wikilinks]] if enabled above), finds attachments not yet tracked or not yet owned by any note, assigns them to this note, then reapplies rules to them.

children.name: Adopt unmanaged attachments in whole vault
children.desc: Same as above, across every note in the vault.

children.name: Auto-reveal active file
children.desc: Automatically reveal the active file in the file explorer when switching files.

children.name: Reveal delay
children.desc: Debounce delay in milliseconds before revealing the file (50–1000).

children.value: This can download and install community plugins. Only use it with trusted vaults, and review your plugin list before enabling auto-install.

children.name: Preview import
children.desc: See which plugins would be installed, skipped, or updated, and which settings would change — without changing your vault.

children.name: Export plugin setup
children.desc: Save your installed community plugins and their settings into the JSON files in .obsidian.

children.name: Import plugin setup
children.desc: Install plugins from the list file. Enabling and applying settings follow the options below.

children.name: Apply settings
children.desc: Update installed plugins from the settings file without reinstalling them.

children.name: Auto-install plugins on startup
children.desc: When Obsidian starts, install any plugins from your list that are not installed yet.

children.name: Auto-enable plugins after installation
children.desc: Turn plugins on after they are installed.

children.name: Apply settings on installation
children.desc: After installing a plugin, apply its settings from your settings file.

children.name: Merge settings instead of replace
children.desc: Update matching settings and keep the rest. When off, the plugin’s saved settings are replaced entirely.

children.name: Sync settings on every startup
children.desc: Each time Obsidian starts, apply your settings file to installed plugins.

children.name: Logging level
children.desc: How much detail to show in the console if something goes wrong. Leave on Error unless you are troubleshooting.

children.name: Format on save
children.desc: When enabled, the file will be automatically formatted (links replaced) when saving.

children.name: Format delay (ms)
children.desc: Delay in milliseconds before formatting stages. Formatter completion is awaited separately; this delay is not a completion timeout.

children.name: Run Prettier after formatting
children.desc: Run Prettier after link formatting and wait for completion before Linter. Requires a compatible prettier-format plugin. Automatic Linker coordinates saving; current Prettier versions do not need a separate save hook.

children.name: Run Obsidian Linter after formatting
children.desc: Run Obsidian Linter after link formatting and Prettier have completed. Requires a compatible Obsidian Linter plugin. Turn off Linter's own Lint on save when Automatic Linker handles saving.

children.name: Respect 'Folder to create new notes in' setting
children.desc: When enabled, the plugin will use Obsidian's 'Folder to create new notes in' setting as the base directory for omitting folder prefixes in links.

children.name: Normalize existing wikilinks
children.desc: When enabled, formatting also normalizes existing wikilinks, such as converting [[pages/Topic|Topic]] to [[Topic]] when the shorter link resolves safely.

children.name: Proximity-based linking
children.desc: When enabled, the plugin will automatically resolve namespaces for shorthand links. If multiple candidates share the same shorthand, the candidate with the most common path segments relative to the current file will be selected.

children.name: Include aliases
children.desc: When enabled, aliases will be included when processing links. Note: A restart is required for changes to take effect.

children.name: Remove aliases in directories
children.desc: Directories where link aliases should be removed, one per line (e.g. 'dir' will convert [[dir/xxx|yyy]] to [[dir/xxx]]). This affects both auto-generated aliases and frontmatter aliases.

children.name: Ignore case
children.desc: When enabled, link matching will be case-insensitive. The original case of the text will be preserved in the link.

children.name: Match sentence case
children.desc: When 'Ignore case' is OFF, match text that is capitalized at the start of a sentence. For example, 'My name' at a sentence start will match the file 'my name'. This setting is ignored when 'Ignore case' is ON.

children.name: Prevent self-linking
children.desc: When enabled, text will not be linked to its own file. For example, the word 'VPN' inside VPN.md will not be converted to a link.

children.name: Ignore date formats
children.desc: When enabled, links that match date formats (e.g. 2025-02-10) will be ignored. This helps maintain compatibility with Obsidian Tasks.

children.name: Ignore headings
children.desc: When enabled, headings (lines starting with #) will not have links added to them.

children.name: Ignore Markdown tables
children.desc: When enabled, Markdown table rows will not have links added to them.

children.name: Exclude directories from automatic linking
children.desc: Directories to be excluded from automatic linking, one per line (e.g. 'Templates')

children.name: Format GitHub URLs on save
children.desc: When enabled, GitHub URLs will be formatted when saving the file.

children.name: GitHub Enterprise URLs
children.desc: Add your GitHub Enterprise URLs, one per line (e.g. github.enterprise.com)

children.name: Format JIRA URLs on save
children.desc: When enabled, JIRA URLs will be formatted when saving the file.

children.name: JIRA URLs
children.desc: Add your JIRA URLs, one per line (e.g. jira.enterprise.com)

children.name: Format Linear URLs on save
children.desc: When enabled, Linear URLs will be formatted when saving the file.

children.name: Replace URL with title
children.desc: When enabled, raw URLs will be replaced with [Page Title](URL). Requires fetching the URL content.

children.name: Ignore domains
children.desc: Ignore domains for replacing URLs with titles, one per line (e.g. x.com)

children.name: Show load notice
children.desc: Display a notice when markdown files are loaded.

children.name: Debug mode
children.desc: When enabled, debug information will be logged to the console.

children.name: Quick setup: paste a blob SAS URL
children.desc: In the Azure portal, open your storage account → Containers → your container → Shared access tokens. Tick Read, Add, Create, Write, Delete and List, pick an expiry date, click "Generate SAS token and URL" and paste the "Blob SAS URL" here to fill in the fields below.

children.name: Storage account name
children.desc: The name of your storage account, e.g. "mystorageaccount".

children.name: Container name
children.desc: The blob container that stores the vault, e.g. "obsidian". It must already exist.

children.name: SAS token
children.desc: The SAS token (sv=…&sig=…). Stored in Obsidian's secret storage on this device, not in the plugin's data file.

children.name: Remote folder
children.desc: Optional folder inside the container for this vault, e.g. "vaults/personal". Leave empty to use the container root. Lets several vaults share one container.

children.name: Blob service URL (advanced)
children.desc: Leave empty for normal Azure accounts. Set it for sovereign clouds, custom domains, private endpoints or the Azurite emulator, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:10000/devstoreaccount1.

children.name: Test connection
children.desc: Checks that the container can be listed, written, read and deleted with this SAS token.

children.name: Live sync
children.desc: Upload changes a few seconds after you edit, check Azure for changes from other devices regularly, and sync on startup. Test the connection first.

options.label: Upload only (back up this vault, never change local files)
Download only (mirror the container, never change the container)

children.name: When a file changed on both sides
children.desc: Applies when the same file was edited here and on another device since the last sync.

options.label: Keep both (save the other version as a conflict copy)

children.name: Upload delay (seconds)
children.desc: How long to wait after the last edit before uploading.

children.name: Check for remote changes every (seconds)
children.desc: How often to look for changes made on other devices. 0 turns polling off (sync then runs on startup, when Obsidian regains focus, and manually). Each check is one cheap list request.

children.name: Sync on startup
children.desc: Run a full sync when Obsidian starts (only with live sync enabled).

children.name: Sync settings folder
children.desc: Also sync the ".obsidian" folder (settings, themes, snippets, plugins). Workspace layout files and this plugin's own settings are never synced. Changes there are picked up by the periodic check.

children.name: Ignore patterns
children.desc: One pattern per line. "*.tmp" or "drafts" match a name in any folder, "Private/" a folder, "/Archive" is anchored at the vault root, "**" matches across folders. Hidden files and folders are always ignored.

children.name: Maximum file size (MB)
children.desc: Larger files are skipped. 0 means no limit.

children.name: Notify on every change
children.desc: Show a notice whenever a sync uploads or downloads files. Errors and conflicts are always shown.

children.name: Sync now
children.desc: Run a full sync right away.Live sync is off

children.name: Reset sync state
children.desc: Forget what was synced before. The next sync compares every file by content: identical files are kept, files that differ are handled as conflicts, nothing is deleted.

children.name: Move branches together
children.desc: When dragging a parent node, move all descendants with it while preserving their relative positions. Disabled by default; enable it here or from the command palette.

children.desc: Alt is recommended. Shift also triggers Obsidian's native horizontal/vertical movement constraint.

children.name: Focus mode
children.desc: Show the current node, all upstream ancestors, and its direct siblings based on every Canvas edge. Downstream nodes are hidden. The Canvas file is not modified.

children.name: Knowledge chain mode
children.desc: In focus mode, show every upstream ancestor and downstream descendant connected to the current node. Sibling branches and unrelated nodes remain hidden.

children.desc: Show branch-copy buttons in the ribbon and Canvas card toolbar. The button copies the selected node, every downstream node along all from → to edges, and all connecting edges, including collapsed nodes.

children.name: Explicit hierarchy and collapse
children.desc: Mark parent → child relations from the native controls for a selected edge, then collapse descendants using those marked relations.

children.name: Automatically mark sibling edges

You are an expert English writing assistant. Your task is to analyze the user's text.
1. Identify any grammar, spelling, or punctuation errors.

{

  "vocabulary": [ { "word": "word/phrase", "meaning": "concise definition", "context": "example sentence based on user context" } ]
}

With the Folder Notes plugin, clicking an album's folder opens its note. Turn off to keep albums side by side in the album folder and songs in the song folder.

children.name: Song folder
children.desc: Where new song notes are created when album notes aren't folder notes. Leave empty for the vault root.

children.name: Album cover folder
children.desc: Where album covers are saved. Leave empty to follow your attachment folder setting.

children.name: Artist photo folder
children.desc: Where artist photos are saved. Leave empty to follow your attachment folder setting.

children.name: Link artists
children.desc: Write an album's artists as [[wikilinks]] when a note with that name already exists. An album never creates its artist's note: add the artist yourself, and the next albums link to it.

children.name: Link genres
children.desc: The same for an album's genres. Off by default: genre notes become very busy hubs.

children.name: Show titles in Latin letters
children.desc: Show an album's and its tracks' titles in Latin letters on the panels — romaji where MusicBrainz has it, English otherwise — for albums added from now on with a title in another script, such as Japanese. The notes themselves stay as they are.

children.name: Name new notes in Latin letters
children.desc: Give new album and song notes with a title in another script their title in Latin letters, as their name and title. Their own title is kept in original_title and aliases, so a search in either finds them. Notes already in your vault are never renamed.

children.name: Show tracklist
children.desc: Below an album's properties, list its tracks.

children.name: Show discography
children.desc: Below an artist's properties, list their albums that are in your vault, with a button to add another.

children.name: Show lyrics
children.desc: Below a song's properties, show its lyrics from LRCLIB, with a button to copy them into the note. Off, nothing is ever sent to LRCLIB.

children.name: Show soundtracks
children.desc: Below a film's, a TV series', an anime's or a game's properties, list the albums linked as its soundtrack, with a button to find another.

children.name: Show scores
children.desc: Below an artist's discography, list the films, TV series, anime and games in your vault they scored: named among a film's composers, or linked from one of their albums as its soundtrack.

children.name: Game folder
children.desc: Where new game notes are created. Leave empty for the vault root.

children.name: Game cover folder
children.desc: Where game covers are saved. Leave empty to follow your attachment folder setting.

children.name: Link developers
children.desc: Write a game's developers and publishers as [[wikilinks]] when a note with that name already exists, so the game shows up in the studio's backlinks.

children.name: Platforms to list

children.name: Short platform names
children.desc: PS4 and Switch rather than PlayStation 4 and Nintendo Switch.

children.name: Only my platforms
children.desc: List only the platforms you play on, in your order, rather than every one a game came out on.

children.name: Show DLCs
children.desc: Below a game's properties, list the DLCs and expansions added to it, each with a checkbox, and a button to add another.

children.name: Book folder
children.desc: Where new book notes are created. Leave empty for the vault root.

children.name: Book cover folder
children.desc: Where book covers are saved. Leave empty to follow your attachment folder setting.

children.name: Author folder
children.desc: Where new author notes are created. Leave empty for the vault root.

children.name: Author photo folder
children.desc: Where author photos are saved. Leave empty to follow your attachment folder setting.

children.name: Link authors
children.desc: Write a book's authors as [[wikilinks]] when a note with that name already exists, so the book shows up in the author's backlinks. A book never creates its author's note: add the author yourself, and the next books link to it.

children.name: Link genres
children.desc: The same for a book's genres. Off by default: genre notes become very busy hubs.

children.name: Show bibliography
children.desc: Below an author's properties, list their books that are in your vault, with a button to add another.

children.name: Import from Goodreads
children.desc: On Goodreads, open My Books, then "Import and export", export your library, and drag goodreads_library_export.csv into your vault. This creates a note for each book not already in your vault, in the folder of its first shelf of your own, with the edition you shelved, your shelves, the day you read it and how many times. Ratings and reviews are not imported.

filters:

children.name: Run rollover
children.desc: Copy unfinished tasks and pins from the previous daily note into the latest one. Skips if already rolled over (unless the mark is stale). Also refreshes routine streaks and pagination.

children.name: Force re-run rollover
children.desc: Clear the saved pair state, then add only tasks that are not already in today's todo (no duplicates). Also refreshes routine streaks, pins, and pagination.

children.name: Target Heading
children.desc: Section label for todos. Written as an h4 heading (#### todo). Also matches a plain 'todo' line in older notes. Scope ends at the first blank line after content.

children.name: Section heading level
children.desc: Markdown heading level used when writing routine / pins / todo / modified / memo / pagination (default 4 → ####).

children.name: Daily Notes Folder
children.desc: Only files in this folder are treated as daily notes.

children.name: Create delay (ms)
children.desc: Wait after file create so the daily template can finish writing before rollover / routine updates.

children.name: Wait for Obsidian Sync
children.desc: Before auto/manual rollover, wait until Sync is idle so the previous daily note is complete. Prevents rolling from a stale note on another device after the date changes.

children.name: Sync wait timeout (ms)
children.desc: Give up waiting for Sync after this many milliseconds (default 120000). Auto rollover is skipped on timeout.

children.name: Sync settle (ms)
children.desc: Extra quiet period after Sync reports idle, so late downloads can finish before reading daily notes.

children.name: Daily Note Format
children.desc: Filename date format for daily notes (moment.js format).

children.name: Tag Date Format
children.desc: Date format used for rollover task tags.

children.name: Update routine streaks
children.desc: Recalculate ⚡consec↑max on the latest daily note from the previous day's check state.

children.name: Routine Heading
children.desc: Section label for routines, written as #### routine. Scope ends at the first blank line after content. Tasks need {id} like {wk}.

children.name: Collect edited notes
children.desc: Automatically add wikilinks under the edited heading when a note is created or modified today. Uses frontmatter created/updated when present, so Sync downloads of old notes are ignored.

children.name: Update edited links
children.desc: Scan the vault and refresh today's daily note with notes whose created or updated date is today.

children.name: Edited Heading
children.desc: Section label written as #### modified. Links are collected on the following lines, until a blank line or a non-link line (such as #### memo).

children.name: Edited debounce (ms)
children.desc: Wait this long after the last create/modify before writing the daily note, so bursts of edits become one write.

children.name: Exclude daily notes
children.desc: Do not list files in the Daily Notes folder (avoids rollover/streak writes showing up as edited notes).

children.name: Ignore folders
children.desc: One vault-relative folder path per line. Notes in these folders are never added to edited.

children.name: Roll over pins
children.desc: Copy wikilinks under the pins heading from the previous daily note into the latest one. Existing pins are kept; duplicates are skipped.

children.name: Roll over pins now
children.desc: Copy pins from the previous daily note into the latest one.

children.name: Pins Heading
children.desc: Section label written as #### pins. Wikilinks under it are carried into the next daily note.

children.name: Link adjacent daily notes
children.desc: Place #### pagination at the top of the daily note (just after frontmatter), with prev : / next : wikilinks to the previous and next existing daily notes (not necessarily yesterday/tomorrow).

children.name: Update pagination now
children.desc: Rewrite pagination on the latest daily note and its neighbors.

children.name: Pagination Heading
children.desc: Section label at the top of the daily note, written as #### pagination. Body is prev : [[date]] and next : [[date]].

control.value:
# Marvis — Coding-agent guide

This folder is a **Marvis project**. Tasks, milestones, logs, and the archive
are real markdown notes managed by the Marvis Obsidian plugin. The folder has
been symlinked into a code repo so coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, …) can
read and edit them directly.

You should read this file before starting any work in this project, and read
every other `.md` in this `skills/` folder for project-specific knowledge.

## Folder layout

- `_project.md` — project metadata (`kind: project`).
- `tasks/*.md` — open tasks (`kind: task`).
- `milestones/*.md` — milestones (`kind: milestone`).
- `logs/*.md` — time-stamped log entries (`kind: log`); filename is the
  timestamp `YYYY-MM-DD-HH-mm-ss.md`.
- `events/*.md` — calendar entries (`kind: event`); filename is
  `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`. May be recurring via an iCal RRULE.
- `archive/*.md` — completed/archived items. **Do not unarchive without an
  explicit user request.**
- `skills/*.md` — agent guidance (you are reading one of these). Add more
  here for project-specific conventions.

## Frontmatter — exact shapes

### Task (`kind: task`)

```yaml
---
kind: task
project: "[[<project-folder-name>]]"   # required
milestone: "[[<milestone-name>]]"      # optional
status: backlog | todo | in-progress | review | blocked | done
priority: low | medium | high          # optional
due: 2026-05-12                        # YYYY-MM-DD, optional
start: 2026-05-01                      # YYYY-MM-DD, optional
tags: [bug, auth]
created: 2026-05-01
order: 1.5                             # fractional sort key, optional
parent: "[[<parent-task>]]"            # optional, for subtasks
recurrence: "every week"               # optional
archived: false                        # set true and move to archive/ when done
---
```

### Milestone (`kind: milestone`)

```yaml
---
kind: milestone
project: "[[<project>]]"
status: planned | active | done
start: 2026-05-01    # optional
due:   2026-06-01
---
```

### Log (`kind: log`)

```yaml
---
kind: log
project: "[[<project>]]"
timestamp: 2026-05-12T14:33:07
tags: [agent]
created: 2026-05-12
---
```

Body is freeform markdown — embeds (`![[file.png]]`, `![[clip.mp3]]`) work.

### Event (`kind: event`)

Calendar-style entries. Live in `events/*.md` under each project folder
(or under the catch-all `_project/events/` if no project is set). Filename
convention: `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`.

```yaml
---
kind: event
project: "[[<project>]]"          # optional; "_project" is the default
title: "Standup"
date: 2026-05-12                  # required, YYYY-MM-DD
time: "10:00"                     # optional; omit for all-day
endTime: "10:30"                  # optional
recurrence: "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE"   # optional, RFC 5545 RRULE
tags: [meeting]
extId: "abc123@google.com"        # optional, set when imported from a feed
source: "google:user@x.com"       # optional, only set by importers
created: 2026-05-12
---
```

- Recurrence is an iCal RRULE string — same format Google Calendar API and
  Microsoft Graph emit. One file per series; views expand occurrences only
  within the visible range.
- Events render in Calendar, Timeline and the Events table — never in
  Kanban (events aren't workflow items).
- A timed event without `endTime` is treated as a point in time. With
  `endTime`, it has a duration in the calendar tooltip.
- Body is freeform markdown — same embedding rules as logs.
- Events with `source: macos:*` are managed by Marvis's calendar sync
  from Apple Calendar (which mirrors any account configured in macOS:
  Exchange, iCloud, Google, etc.). Editing them by hand may be overwritten
  on the next sync. Hand-authored events have no `source` field and are
  never touched by sync.

## Wikilink rules

- Use the **bare folder/file name** in wikilinks: `[[marvis]]`, not
  `[[Marvis/marvis/_project]]`.
- No `.md` extension.
- The plugin parses the inner text via `stripWikilink`; pathy links work but
  bare names are preferred.

## How to pick a task

1. List `tasks/*.md`.
2. Filter: `status` not `done`, `archived` not `true`.
3. Sort: priority (`high` > `medium` > `low`), then `due` ascending,
   then `order` ascending.
4. Show the user the candidates by title; ask them to pick before doing work.
5. Read the picked task's full body before you start.
6. **Add `by-AI` to the task's `tags`** (if not already there). This lets the
   user filter for AI-touched tasks later. Preserve all other existing tags.
7. Set `status: in-progress` (regardless of prior status — see note below).
8. **Append a plan section to the task body** before writing any code:

   ```markdown
   ## Plan — 2026-05-02 20:30 (by-AI)

   <2–6 bullet points on the approach, files to touch, and any open assumptions>
   ```

   Keep it tight — concrete enough to execute against, short enough to scan.

**Picking a task in a non-default state:** the user may hand you a task that's
already `in-progress`, `blocked`, or even `done` (e.g. for a follow-up). The
intake is still the same — add `by-AI` to tags, append a fresh `## Plan —
<timestamp> (by-AI)` section, and set `status: in-progress` if it isn't
already there. Don't skip the plan just because the task wasn't in `todo`.

## How to update task state

- Edit only the `---` frontmatter block of the task — don't rewrite the
  existing body unless the user asks. The body is the user's task description.
  You may **append** new headings (Plan, Update, Blocked) without touching what
  was already there.
- When you start: `status: in-progress`.
- When you finish: `status: review` (not `done`) **and append a work-summary
  section to the task's body** (see "Recording work on a task"). The user
  reviews the change and flips it to `done` themselves; never set `done`
  yourself unless the user explicitly tells you to.
- Status flow: `backlog → todo → in-progress → review → done`. `blocked` is
  a side-state used when you genuinely can't proceed.
- Never invent a status or priority value. Use what's already in use across
  the project, or the canonical set above.

## When the task is vague or under-specified

Try to complete it autonomously first. Use the title, body, surrounding code,
and the rest of this skills folder to make a reasonable interpretation. Only
stop if you genuinely cannot proceed without input the codebase doesn't have.

If you're truly blocked:

1. Set `status: blocked`.
2. Append a Blocked section to the task body explaining what's missing:

   ```markdown
   ## Blocked — 2026-05-02 20:30 (by-AI)

   <what you understood the task to be>

   **Need from user:** <specific question(s) or missing decision(s)>

   <what you tried before stopping, if anything>
   ```

   Be specific — a question the user can answer in one sentence beats a vague
   "needs more info." Don't set `blocked` for trivial ambiguity you can resolve
   yourself; that's just noise.

## Recording work on a task

When you finish (or pause meaningfully) a task, **append** to the task's body
under a heading so the user can see what you did:

```markdown
## Update — 2026-05-02 20:30 (by-AI)

<one or two sentences on what you changed>

- file/path/one.ts
- file/path/two.tsx
```

Use a fresh `## Update — <timestamp> (by-AI)` heading per session so multiple
updates accumulate. Keep it short — link to files, not full diffs.

## When to write a log entry

Logs are for project-wide events, **not** routine task completions. Write a
log only when:

- You make a non-obvious decision that spans multiple tasks (library choice,
  design tradeoff, blocking issue).
- The user explicitly asks you to record something.

Filename = current local timestamp `YYYY-MM-DD-HH-mm-ss.md` (must match
`timestamp:` to the second). Body is freeform. **Always include `by-AI` in
`tags`**.

## Hard rules

- **Don't unarchive** anything in `archive/` without explicit confirmation.
- **Don't touch other projects** in the surrounding `Marvis/` (you only
  see this one via the symlink).
- **Don't write secrets** (tokens, API keys, passwords) into any task or log
  body. If the user shares one for context, omit it from anything you save.
- **Don't delete** files. Archive (frontmatter flag + folder move) instead.
- **Don't rename `_project.md`** or change the project's folder name —
  that's the project's identity.

## Adding more skills

If a project needs deeper conventions (database schema, API contract, naming
rules), create another `.md` next to this one and explain them. Keep
`marvis.md` focused on the universal Marvis conventions.

# MD 排版美化器 - 规则模板
# 修改后保存，立即生效

heading:
  minLevel: 2          # 最低从 H2 开始
  maxLevel: 6
  blankBefore: 1       # 标题前空行数
  blankAfter: 1        # 标题后空行数
  forbidSkip: true     # 禁止标题跳级

list:
  unorderedMarker: "-"  # 无序列表符号：- / * / +
  indent: 2             # 缩进空格数
  blankBetweenItems: false  # 列表项间是否空行

codeBlock:
  fenceStyle: "```"  # 围栏符号
  blankAround: 1        # 前后空行数

table:
  alignColumns: true    # 对齐列宽
  padding: 1            # 列内边距空格数

blockquote:
  blankAround: 1        # 前后空行数
  mergeAdjacent: true   # 合并相邻引用块

horizontalRule:
  style: "---"          # --- / *** / ___
  blankAround: 1

spacing:
  paragraphGap: 1       # 段落间空行数
  chineseEnglishSpace: true  # 中英文间自动加空格
  trimTrailing: true    # 去除行尾空格

link:
  style: "inline"       # inline / reference

frontMatter:
  preserve: true        # 保留 YAML front matter
  blankAfter: 1         # front matter 后空行数

children.value: How to add your custom SVG icons:
Find your Obsidian vault folder on your device
Navigate to the hidden .obsidian folder inside your vault
Go to .obsidian/plugins/my-svgs/icons/ folder (create the icons folder if it doesn't exist)
Copy your SVG files into this folder
Click the "Reload Now" button to load your new icons
Your icons will appear in the grid below after reloading
Each icon will be named as my-filename (example: if your file is home.svg, the icon will be my-home)

If you don't see your icons, click the "Reload Now" button above the grid

children.name: Verse offset
children.desc: Change this if wrong verses are being linked, e.g. you want "Gen 1,1-3" but output is text from verses 2-4 → set this to -1

children.name: Verse heading level
children.desc: If set, only headings of specified level are considered verses (if first heading of this level is always a verse, also set "Verse offset" to -1)

children.name: Line prefix
children.desc: String inserted in front of every line, for example '>' for quote. Note: If you set 'Put each verse on a new line?' to true, the prefix will be inserted in front of every line.

children.name: Link postfix
children.desc: String inserted after biblical link, you can use \n to insert newline. If you are using multiple translations "{t}" will insert the name of the one used.

children.name: Each verse prefix
children.desc: String inserted in front of every copied verse. You can use "{n}" where you want number of given verse inserted, for example "**{n}** " will make each verse start with bold verse number. You can also use "{f}" to insert name of the corresponding file (for example to create obsidian links). If you are using multiple translations "{t}" will insert the name of the one used. "{u}" will insert the number of the verse as unicode superscript. Leave empty for no prefix.

children.name: Each verse postfix
children.desc: String inserted at the end of every copied verse. You can use "{n}" where you want number of given verse inserted, for example "**{n}** " will make each verse start with bold verse number. You can also use "{f}" to insert name of the corresponding file (for example to create obsidian links). If you are using multiple translations "{t}" will insert the name of the one used. "{u}" will insert the number of the verse as unicode superscript. Leave empty for no postfix.

children.name: Output book name convertor
children.desc: You can specify conversions that will be applied to the visible book name alias. For example, if you put in "3J:3 John", the output will be changed from "[[3 John-01#v1|3J 1.1]]" to "[[3 John-01#v1|3 John 1.1]]". The format used is "From:To", each entry on it's own line. TIP: ChatGPT (or similar AI tool) will probably be able to help you when creating the input.

For example, if you put in "Gn:Gen", the input "Gn 1,1" will work even when the file is called "Gen 1,1". The format used is again "From:To", each entry on it's own line, and will be used by the plugin when the search fails using the unchanged input. Multiple entries can have same result mapping, for example you can use "G:Gen" and "Gn:Gen".

control.value:
<!-- Outcrop head snippet — injected into <head> on every public note page.
     Use it for fonts, verification meta tags, a favicon, etc.

     The default theme's fonts, loaded from Google Fonts as variable fonts
     (one file per family/style covers the whole 400–700 weight range, which
     is how the body renders at a true 450):
       Google Sans (body), Google Sans Code (code), Crimson Pro italic (titles).
     Swap the families here and update the --font-* tokens in the Site CSS
     to change them. The server's Content-Security-Policy allows styles and
     fonts only from fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com — external

<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>

children.desc: Also asks a calibrated model whether the cited title and the resolved title describe the same work. Catches a one-word swap in a long title that character similarity misses. A flagged citation is reported as ambiguous for review, never as a fabrication. The judgment is not byte-repeatable on borderline titles.

Things that already happen every week. Drawn behind the grid and subtracted from availability before "Fit this week" proposes anything — not editable from the grid itself yet.

When work could happen — not what's already booked, but where there's room for it. A window's name is matched against a #tag on a task (a window named "content" claims a task tagged #content first); an untagged task can land in any window. Without at least one window here, "Fit this week" has nowhere to propose anything.

How long an un-annotated task takes, by its #tag. This is what makes Weekfit work on a vault where nothing is annotated: every task is sized by a ladder — an estimate written on the line itself, beats its #tag’s default below, beats the global fallback — so nothing needs a hand-typed estimate to be fitted.
